title.narrative: SET-UP, LAUNCH OF THE CODEO NATIONAL INFORMATION CENTER (NIC), VISITS TO THE NIC AND SIMULATION EXERCISES

description.narrative: One week before the election, the CODEO Secretariat moved its activities to the Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Center (KAIPTC). The KAIPTC served as CODEO’s National Information Center (NIC) where the Board, Secretariat staff, and Data Entry Clerks were stationed for the duration of the election day, until the final presidential results were declared by the Chairperson of the Electoral Commission. The set-up of the NIC comprised the following: a PVT room containing 20 laptops and cell phones, an incident desk room containing 10 laptops, a media room, rooms for study missions, and breakout rooms for the CODEO Advisory Board. At the NIC, CODEO expanded its incident desk by collaborating with Penplusbytes to fact-check incidents. CODEO expanded its incident desk by collaborating with Penplusbytes to fact-check incidents. The purpose of fact-checking was to counter misinformation that could arise on election day. The NIC was successfully launched on December 6, 2024, with good participation from media houses, representatives from security agencies, state agencies, political parties, members of the diplomatic corps, development partners, and relevant stakeholders in attendance. Following the launch of the NIC, several dignitaries, both local and international, were given a tour of the NIC. The NIC was the go-to center for independent, unbiased, non-partisan, and objective assessment of the electoral process in the country.

activity-date.narrative: Following the launch of the National Information Center (NIC) at the Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Center (KAIPTC) on December 6, 2024, the NIC was opened to the public. From the 6th through to the 8th of December, several high-profile individuals and delegations visited the NIC to observe the activities of CODEO during the elections. The NIC received diplomats, including the Netherlands Ambassador to Ghana, UK High Commissioner to Ghana, the US Ambassador to Ghana, accompanied by a delegation from the US Embassy and USAID. Delegations from the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), European Union, the German Embassy, and the Embassies of the Czech Republic, and Austria were also present during the period. Other prominent organizations such as the International Republican Institute (IRI), the International Foundation for Electoral Systems (IFES), YIAGA Africa, East and Horn of Africa Election Observers Network (E-HORN), the West Africa Democracy Solidarity Network (WADEMOS) and the NDI study group, also visited to engage with and understand CODEO’s operations at the NIC. Distinguished individuals who visited the NIC included Dr. Ibn Chambass, and former Nigerian President Goodluck Jonathan, who led the West Africa Elders Forum, Chair of the Commonwealth Dr. Masisi, former President of Botswana, and the Special Representative of the UN to West Africa. As part of the protocol, each delegation was given a guided tour of the various sections of the NIC.

On election day, observers reported to their assigned polling stations and observed proceedings from the start of polls, through to closing, counting and declaration of results at their assigned polling stations. They completed and submitted reports on the checklist at scheduled periods throughout the polls and also submitted critical incident reports as and when an incident occurred at their assigned polling stations. All observers sent observation data through a short code via SMS into the CODEO Observation database.
As part of our mission to promote transparency, and credibility and allow for the free flow of up-to-date information to our stakeholders throughout the election period, the Coalition organized four (4) press encounters and published six (6) observation reports during the 2024 Presidential and Parliamentary Elections. The first press briefing was held on December 6, 2024, at the Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Center (KAIPTC), where the National Information Center (NIC) was based. The briefing provided detailed plans for the Coalition’s observation of the elections on December 7, which included the deployment of 4,000 observers nationwide. This encounter also served as the official launch of the NIC. On December 7, 2024, CODEO held a midday press conference to provide updates on the voting process. This was to report on parts of the electoral process such as the setup and opening of polling stations, the presence of election materials, the accessibility of polling stations, and the conduct of election stakeholders from the morning of December 7 through to midday. On December 7, 2024, a close of polls statement was also released. CODEO presented a preliminary post-election report during a press encounter at the NIC on December 8. This report provided an update on election day activities, including the participation of party agents, the functioning of polling stations, and the collation processes and the PVT results on voter turnout and rejected ballots. Following the Electoral Commission’s declaration of official presidential election results on December 9, 2024, the Coalition organized a final press conference at the CDD-Ghana Conference Room on the evening of December 9 to validate the EC’s results, using our PVT estimates.
The PVT findings confirmed that the official partial results were consistent with CODEO’s independent estimates, providing reassurance to the public and stakeholders about the credibility of the process. CODEO verified the results released by the Electoral Commission that declared the flagbearer of the main opposition party as President-elect (excluding the results from 9 constituencies) and requested the EC to recheck their incorrect turnout figures . CODEO reached out to EC ahead of its PVT statement to alert them of the mistake. The EC indicated that they would correct it when they get their final results. CODEO went ahead to release its statement and did note the EC’s turnout figure as incorrect. CODEO indicated it would do its final verification when the EC releases the full data.
